events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven.** I'd rate its pier **2 (average)** this week, the highest of the four.
- **Muskegon: 1 (below average).** Pier fishing has been slow there.
- **South Haven: 1 (below average), low confidence.** No pier report in the last four weeks.
- **St. Joseph: 1 (below average), low confidence.** No pier report in the last four weeks.
- If you fish Grand Haven, start with glow spoons or live bait (gizzard shad or alewives) at the pierheads, around 70 ft of water.

## Why

- Grand Haven's pier was the only one of the four with a good pier report recently: the Aug 26 report rated it good (3) when the water had just dropped sharply.
- Pier fishing was slow at Grand Haven and Muskegon on Sept 2 and Sept 9, when the buoy water was 70-71 F, so I'd expect pier results to stay weak until the water cools.
- The buoys now show sharp drops of 10-17 F, and I'd expect that upwelling to bring some fish to the piers, which is why I rated Grand Haven at 2 instead of 1.
- The Sept 9 report was the newest pier report for St. Joseph and South Haven, and it has no pier data, so their 1s rest on history and the lack of recent reports.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest report 2026-09-09, 13 days old)
- Grand Haven, 2026-08-26: pier rated 3. "Salmon were caught from the pierheads in 70 feet of water… Glow spoons, glow plugs, and white flies were all productive." Live bait (gizzard shad, alewives) also worked.
- Grand Haven, 2026-09-02: pier rated 0. "Pier anglers targeting salmon reported very slow action due to increased water temperatures."
- Grand Haven, 2026-09-09: pier not rated. Boats did well: "Salmon action was good for boat anglers 65 to 100 feet down in 85 to 140 feet of water."
- Muskegon, 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-09: pier rated 0 both times. Sept 9: "Pier anglers were unsuccessful targeting salmon due to warm water temperatures."
- Muskegon, 2026-08-26: pier rated 1; a few Chinook on glow spoons.
- St. Joseph (2026-09-09) and South Haven (2026-09-09): only boat and river reports, no pier reports. St. Joseph's boat bite was at about 40 ft and 120 ft; South Haven's boat anglers caught only "a few" fish inside 100 ft.

**Past seasons** (history, similar water temperature near 61 F, 2022-2025)
- Pier fishing at these ports was usually slow or average: Grand Haven 2024-10-02 (0), Muskegon 2024-09-11 (1), South Haven 2024-09-11 (0) and 2024-10-02 (1), St. Joseph 2023-10-04 (0) and 2023-10-11 (0).
- Grand Haven 2024-09-11 is the one history case of pier fish on alewives and glow spoons during an upwelling, with ratings not given.

**Conditions now** (measured buoy surface water, with change over the prior week)
- St. Joseph 59 F (down 11 F), South Haven 61 F (down 17 F), Grand Haven 65 F (down 10 F), Muskegon 65 F (down 10 F). The tool flagged possible upwelling at all four.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension): north or east winds push warm water offshore and cold water up along the shore, bringing salmon toward pierheads and river mouths. A sharp buoy drop is the sign of this.

## Caveats

- The newest pier reports are 13 days old. The fall season is changing quickly, so these ratings are estimates.
- The current-conditions tool returned a backtest summary, not live readings, and gave no modeled pierhead temperature. I can't confirm the upwelling is still happening today; check the pierhead water temperature before you go.
- St. Joseph and South Haven have no pier reports in the last four weeks, so those 1 ratings rest on history and boat reports.
- Grand Haven's good pier report (Aug 26) is 4 weeks old, and the two later reports there were slow.

## Sources

- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Sept 9 2026: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/4292fc6
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Sept 2 2026: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/4280cb4
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Aug 26 2026: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/426de2b
- Grand Haven, Muskegon, and South Haven, Sept 11 2024: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b5093d
